name: NASA Open APIs (APOD, NeoWs, EPIC, DONKI)
summary: Collection of NASA APIs: Astronomy Picture of the Day, near-Earth objects, EPIC Earth imagery, DONKI space weather and more.
description: One api.nasa.gov key unlocks many endpoints: APOD (daily astronomy image with explanation), NeoWs (near-Earth asteroid feed and lookup), DONKI (solar flares, CMEs, geomagnetic storms), EPIC (full-disc Earth imagery), Mars rover photos, TechTransfer and more. The shared key DEMO_KEY works without signup at low limits.

auth.notes: Free signup at api.nasa.gov; DEMO_KEY works for testing at low limits.

rate_limit.summary: DEMO_KEY: 30 requests/hour and 50/day per IP (documented); a registered free key: 1,000 requests/hour. x-ratelimit-limit: 10 was observed on DEMO_KEY.

example.response_excerpt:
{
  "date": "2026-11-10",
  "title": "NASA Science",
  "media_type": "image",
  "url": "https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/themes/nasa-child/assets/images/nasa-logo@2x.png",
  "explanation": "Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way, is about 100,000 light years across..."
}

license.name: Mostly public domain; individual APOD images may carry copyright

coverage.geographic: Global, plus solar and near-Earth space data

agent_notes: Register a free key for real use; DEMO_KEY is heavily rate limited. Pass an explicit date to APOD to avoid empty or transient errors, and check media_type since APOD can be a video.
caveats: APOD sometimes returns video or placeholder content, and individual images may be copyrighted (see the copyright field).
A first request without a date returned HTTP 500 once (transient); retry with an explicit date.
Only APOD was verified directly; other sub-APIs are as per NASA docs.
